target.title: improve(health): surface dead-lettered delivery queue entries
target.body:
**Prompt request:** Make `openclaw health` report deliveries that were dead-lettered by the durable delivery queue, so silent message loss becomes visible, while keeping the queue's enqueue, retry, and recovery behavior unchanged.

**Proof target:** Show that dead-lettered entries surface in the health snapshot (JSON field and warning line) and that a queue with only pending entries reports nothing.

## What Problem This Solves

Resolves a problem where messages that permanently fail delivery are invisible to operators. When a delivery exhausts its retries, the durable delivery queue moves the entry to a `failed` status that is retained for diagnostics — but nothing ever reads those rows back: `openclaw health` stays all-green, and the only trace is a gateway log line at the moment it happened. An operator whose channel had an outage has no way to notice that messages were dropped.

## Why This Change Was Made

The SQLite delivery queue already persists dead-lettered entries with a `failed_at` timestamp; the gap is purely read-side. This change adds a per-queue failed-count accessor to the storage layer and reports dead-lettered entries from `getHealthSnapshot`, the builder shared by the gateway health state and the `openclaw health` command. It follows the existing plugin and context-engine health section pattern: the `deliveryQueues` field is omitted when nothing is dead-lettered, a storage read failure degrades to omitting the section rather than failing health, and the text renderer adds one warning line. Because the gateway health handler can serve a cached snapshot for up to a refresh interval, the cached-response merge path recomputes the delivery queue summary the same way it already refreshes context-engine and model-pricing state, so a delivery that dead-letters right after the cache fills is still reported. Observer-only — no retry, purge, or queue behavior change.

## User Impact

Operators now see dead-lettered deliveries in `openclaw health`: a JSON `deliveryQueues.failed` entry per queue (count plus oldest failure timestamp) and a text line such as `Delivery queue: warning (dead-lettered entries — outbound: 2; oldest 2h ago)`. Healthy systems see no new output.

## Evidence

Real-runtime capture using the production storage layer with no mocks (isolated `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR`; three outbound deliveries enqueued via `upsertDeliveryQueueEntry`, two dead-lettered via `moveDeliveryQueueEntryToFailed`, then the real `getHealthSnapshot`):

Before (main):

```
[health-json] deliveryQueues=undefined (field absent)
PROOF: health shows nothing despite dead-lettered deliveries
```

After (this PR):

```
[health-json] deliveryQueues={"failed":[{"queueName":"outbound","count":2,"oldestFailedAt":1783143277568}]}
[health-text] Delivery queue: warning (dead-lettered entries — outbound: 2; oldest 2s ago)
PROOF: dead-lettered deliveries visible in health
```

The still-pending third delivery does not appear — only dead-lettered entries are reported.

Focused tests: `src/infra/delivery-queue-sqlite.test.ts` — an empty queue returns no counts; dead-lettered entries are counted per queue with exact oldest-failure timestamps (fake timers) while pending entries stay excluded. `src/commands/health.snapshot.test.ts` — the built health snapshot omits the field for a clean queue and reports the dead-lettered entry against an isolated state dir. `src/commands/health.test.ts` — `openclaw health` renders the warning line from a gateway summary, and the formatter returns null when nothing is dead-lettered. `src/gateway/server-methods/server-methods.test.ts` — a cached gateway health response reports a delivery dead-lettered after the cache was filled. The new assertions fail without the change.
